summaries.title: How To Screw Up A Secular Bull Market
summaries.reason: Model scores on Aug 14, 2026 confirm the secular bull "unequivocally" and demographics suggest it could run to 2035, but the video is a guardrails piece — it refuses to assume tech keeps leading and stresses risk mitigation, so constructive but cautious.
summaries.summary:
• Model scores on Aug 14, 2026 confirm we are "unequivocally" in a secular bull; demographics make a case it could last until 2035, so the goal is navigating point A to point B without making mistakes.
• Realistic volatility: the 1950 and 1982 secular bulls each saw 16 drawdowns greater than 6% (average ~11.5%, median ~9.6%) — bigger drawdowns are normal, "secular does not mean easy."
• The Nasdaq 100 weekly chart doesn't resemble the 2000 peaking process: consolidation from 2021-2023, a breakout, no extreme extension, and no white space between moving averages.
• Nasdaq 100 vs S&P shows no abnormal outperformance and is only now breaking above a 20+ year consolidation level — the "it looks like 2000" claim is wrong; stay patient above this level.
• Trend strength scores are pinned at 100/100; in strong trends relative charts matter most — short-term Treasuries (SHV) vs S&P just made an all-time low, showing no defensive/fear spike (unlike 2018, COVID, 2025, and 2022).
• Bloomberg's financial conditions index is the loosest since the 1990s — read as stability and confidence, and the 1990s loosening preceded the 1990-2000 rally.
• Six ways to screw up a secular bull (via Munger inversion): overtrading, selling winners too soon ("pulling flowers and watering the weeds"), chasing mean-reversion traps (dumping XLK for RSP/small caps), panicking in mid-cycle pullbacks, over-leveraging/margin, and surrendering to the doom industrial complex.
• Practical rules: stay with long-term leaders, size volatile positions sensibly (e.g., avoid 30-50% SMH concentration), don't demand certainty, and keep mitigation strategies in case the bull ends today.
• If the S&P heads from 7,800 to 10,000 (+28%), the goal is capturing it — avoiding behavioral errors is the edge, while assuming you're wrong and staying flexible daily.
